from build123d import *
import math


def build(p):
    # NOTE: the spec puts a hemispherical cavity (here dia 24) in the centre of the
    # parting face, and the parting_face port origin [0, 0, H/2] sits right
    # over that cavity. So there is no material directly under the port origin.
    # The spec says to keep the stated feature over the assertion, so the
    # cavity stays. The port pose needs fixing in the contract, by the architect.
    L = float(p.length)
    W = float(p.width)
    H = float(p.height)
    cav_r = float(p.cavity_diameter) / 2.0
    dd = float(p.dowels_dowel_d)
    hole_d = dd - 0.05  # FDM press fit
    hole_depth = 5.5
    top = H / 2.0

    # Solid blocky mold half, parting face at z = +H/2
    block = Box(L, W, H)

    # Crisp 0.5 mm chamfer on the outer edges: vertical corners and base edges.
    # The parting (top) face edges stay sharp so the halves seal.
    vert = block.edges().filter_by(Axis.Z)
    bottom = block.edges().group_by(Axis.Z)[0]
    block = chamfer(list(vert) + list(bottom), 0.5)

    # Hemispherical placeholder cavity sunk into the centre of the parting face
    block = block - Pos(0, 0, top) * Sphere(cav_r)

    # Two press-fit dowel holes at x = +/-24 on the parting face
    dx = 24.0
    hole = Cylinder(hole_d / 2.0, hole_depth)
    block = block - [Pos(sx * dx, 0, top - hole_depth / 2.0) * hole for sx in (-1, 1)]

    return block

from build123d import *
import math


def build(p):
    L = p.length
    W = p.width
    H = p.height
    cav_r = p.cavity_diameter / 2.0
    sprue_r = p.sprue_diameter / 2.0
    dowel_cut_r = (p.dowels_dowel_d + 0.15) / 2.0
    dowel_depth = 5.5
    z_part = -H / 2.0

    # Solid block centred on the origin. The parting face is the flat bottom
    # at z = -H/2 and the top face is at +H/2.
    block = Box(L, W, H)

    # 0.5 mm chamfer on the top perimeter only. The parting-face perimeter
    # stays sharp and the bottom face stays a full L x W flat so the halves seal.
    block = chamfer(block.edges().group_by(Axis.Z)[-1], 0.5)

    # NOTE (spec vs probe conflict): the spec puts the hemispherical cavity at
    # the centre of the parting face, so there is no material directly above
    # the parting_face port origin (0, 0, -H/2). The spec is kept as written.
    # The port should be moved off-centre, or declared as an annulus outside
    # the cavity. Also, ring_diameter 52.2 is wider than the 40 mm block width.
    block = block - Pos(0, 0, z_part) * Sphere(cav_r)

    # Pour sprue from the cavity up through the top face
    sprue_len = H + 2.0
    block = block - Pos(0, 0, z_part + sprue_len / 2.0) * Cylinder(sprue_r, sprue_len)

    # Slip-fit dowel holes, 5.5 mm deep from the parting face, at x = +/-24
    hole = Cylinder(dowel_cut_r, dowel_depth)
    block = block - [
        Pos(sx * 24.0, 0, z_part + dowel_depth / 2.0) * hole
        for sx in (-1, 1)
    ]

    return block

from build123d import *
import math

# CONTRACT CONFLICT (for the architect / repair report):
# The spec puts the two blind rod sockets at x = +/-15 (rods 30 mm apart).
# The pinned ports j1_rod and j2_rod both declare origin [0, 0, 10], which is the
# block centre, so both bores land at the same point. The G3 probe looks for a hole
# at x = 0, but this design has no hole there.
# The fix belongs in the contract, not here: j1_rod origin should be [-15, 0, 10]
# and j2_rod origin should be [15, 0, 10]. The geometry below follows the spec and
# does not add a centre hole the spec never asked for.


def build(p):
    w = p.width
    h = p.height
    t = p.thickness
    rod_spacing = 30.0
    floor = 1.2
    depth = t - floor  # blind socket depth from the +z inner face

    # Main block: x across rods, y up from the bench (-y face is the foot), z along the rods.
    block = Box(w, h, t)
    # Small crisp chamfer on all outside edges, matching the carriage. Done before any cuts.
    block = chamfer(block.edges(), 0.8)

    # Blind rod sockets at x = +/-15, rods at mid-height (y = 0), opening on the +z face.
    # Each cutter runs 0.5 mm past the +z face so the opening is clean.
    sockets = []
    for sx, d in ((-1, p.j1_rod_d), (1, p.j2_rod_d)):
        r = d / 2.0
        cut_len = depth + 0.5
        zc = t / 2.0 + 0.5 - cut_len / 2.0
        sockets.append(Pos(sx * rod_spacing / 2.0, 0, zc) * Cylinder(r, cut_len))
    block = block - sockets

    return block

brief.goal: a hand-cranked winch: a printed 120x80x6mm base with two 60mm-tall, 6mm-thick side plates; a crank shaft carrying a 15-tooth module-1.5 spur gear that drives a 45-tooth module-1.5 spur gear on a 30mm-diameter rope drum shaft (3:1 reduction); both shafts turn in 608 bearings in the side plates; a 60mm crank arm with a handle
brief.design: Sturdy utilitarian machine look: flat faces, generous 1 mm chamfers on outside edges, and fillets only where a hand touches (crank handle, arm ends). Bosses and flanges should read as deliberate thick rings rather than thin lips, and every printed part should look like it belongs to one heavy-duty kit.

frame.title: Winch frame
frame.spec: One-piece U-shaped winch frame: a flat 120x80x6 base plate with two 6 mm thick side plates, 60 mm tall, standing along both long edges. Each side plate carries two round bearing bosses on its inner face, one on the drum axis and one on the crank axis, thick enough to hold two 608 bearings and a shoulder. The bosses are the same height and sit level with each other across the gap. The joint rules cut the 608 bearing seats into the bosses. The crank axis sits beside the drum axis at the gear mesh distance.

contract.name: Winch frame
